title: Traumatic brain injury and concussion in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the head injury (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/24/2026
Reason for Admission: Motor vehicle accident with head trauma.

Vitals:
T: 98.4 F, HR: 78 (RRR), BP: 132/80, RR: 16, SpO2: 96% on RA.

Recent Labs:
WBC: 8.2, Hgb: 13.4, Plt: 210, Na: 138, K: 4.1, Cr: 1.1, eGFR: 68.

Review of Systems:
Neuro: Positive for altered mental status, positive for diffuse axonal injury. Negative for focal deficits.
CV: NAD.
Resp: NAD.
GI: NAD.
MSK: Positive for minor bruising on extremities.

Social History: Retired. Lives with spouse. No tobacco use.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had type 2 diabetes.

Hospital Course:
Pt is a 90-year-old male admitted following a car crash. Initial assessment revealed a diffuse brain injury. Pt was unconscious for three days following the impact. During the acute phase, neuro status was monitored closely. Pt eventually returned to his usual level of consciousness. Imaging and clinical monitoring confirmed diffuse axonal injury. During the stay, pt was stable, and there were no major complications. Pt showed gradual improvement in orientation and mobility. Transitioned to physical therapy and nursing care.

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Diffuse axonal injury.
2. Traumatic brain injury.
3. Status post motor vehicle accident.

Discharge Medications:
1. Acetaminophen 650mg BID PRN for pain.
2. Meloxicam 7.5mg daily.
3. Multivitamin daily.

Follow-up:
Pt to f/u with neurology in 1 week. Pt to f/u with primary care physician in 2 weeks. Pt instructed to monitor for any changes in mental status or increased headache.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, MD, 05/24/2026
explanations: Diffuse traumatic brain injury with loss of consciousness over 24 hours and return to the prior conscious level, initial encounter: S06.2X5A (HCC 397).

hccs.label: Major Head Injury with Loss of Consciousness > 1 Hour
